name: Ride a unicycle
blurb: Legendarily hard for about fifteen hours and then suddenly fine. There is no technique shortcut — it is pure balance adaptation, measured in hours in the saddle.
gear: A unicycle sized to your inseam
A wall, railing or two helpers
steps: Set the seat height so your leg is nearly straight at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Mount against a wall or railing, sit tall with your weight in the saddle rather than on the pedals.
Ride along a wall, hand trailing, until you can go the length of it consistently.
Practise letting go for one pedal stroke, then two, then more.
Learn to look ahead, not down, and to correct by pedalling rather than by flailing.
Learn the free mount last — it is the hardest part and comes after riding.
tips: Sit down properly. Standing on the pedals is exhausting and unstable.
It really does take about 15 hours of practice before it clicks. Nothing is wrong with you at hour eight.
proof: You free mount and ride 50 metres unaided, then dismount cleanly.
